paper.title: Mock Paper · Primary 3 Language Use and Comprehension (B)
paper.note: The second of three Primary 3 papers, the same length and marks as the first. Leave at least a few days between them, and look at your error log in between.

questions.q: The children ______ their shoes before entering the hall.
There ______ a long queue at the bookshop this morning.
My sister is afraid ______ thunder.
Rahim can run ______ than anyone else in our class.
______ you remember to bring your recorder tomorrow?
The kitten hurt ______ when it jumped off the shelf.
We waited at the gate ______ the rain stopped.
Mrs Lim gave each pupil ______ exercise book.
There are only ______ biscuits left in the tin.
Siti ______ her homework when the lights went out.

sections.name: Booklet A · Vocabulary
sections.instruction: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word in bold.

questions.q: The old bridge was **shaky**, so nobody was allowed to cross it.
Devi **whispered** the answer to her partner.
The puppy looked **miserable** in the rain.
My grandfather **chuckled** at the photograph.
The hall was **packed** on Sports Day.
We had to **hurry** or we would miss the bus.
The soup was **bland**, so Mother added some pepper.
Ravi was **delighted** with his new bicycle.

sections.name: Booklet B · Grammar Cloze
sections.instruction: Fill each blank with one suitable word.
sections.passage:
Our School Garden

Last term our class was given a small plot of land behind the canteen. Mr Devan, our form teacher, said we could grow (1)______ we liked, as long as we looked after it ourselves.

We chose kangkong, because it grows quickly. On the first morning we dug the soil, pulled (2)______ the weeds and made four long rows. By the time the bell rang, every one of us (3)______ covered in mud.

Watering was the hard part. We agreed to come in pairs before school, (4)______ some mornings a pair forgot. Then Lixin made a chart and pinned it (5)______ the classroom door, and after that nobody had an excuse.

Six weeks later the leaves were taller (6)______ my hand. We cut them carefully and carried them to the canteen, (7)______ Auntie Siti cooked them for us at lunch.

It was the best plate of vegetables I (8)______ ever eaten, and I am not usually fond of kangkong.

answers.tip: 'Whatever we liked' — the whole clause is the object of 'grow'.
'Pull out' or 'pull up' the weeds; both are used.
'Every one of us' is singular, and the story is in the past.
The two halves disagree, so a contrast word is needed.
A chart is pinned on or to a door.
'Taller than' — the comparison word after a comparative adjective.
'Where' points back to the canteen, the place Auntie Siti was.
'Had ever eaten' — the past perfect, looking back from that lunch.

sections.name: Booklet B · Spelling and Grammar Editing
sections.instruction: There is one spelling or grammar error in each line. Write the correction — one word only.

questions.q: Last Sunday my family goes to the beach at Pasir Ris.
questions.tip: The error was “goes”. “Last Sunday” is in the past, so the verb must be past too.

questions.q: We arrived their at nine o'clock in the morning.
questions.tip: The error was “their”. “There” means that place; “their” shows belonging.

questions.q: My brother bring a kite with a long red tail.
questions.tip: The error was “bring”. The rest of the story is in the past.

questions.q: My father sat on a mat and read a newspapper.
questions.tip: The error was “newspapper”. There is only one p in the middle of “newspaper”.

questions.q: I builded a sandcastle with my cousin Aisha.
questions.tip: The error was “builded”. The past tense of “build” is “built”.

questions.q: Aisha cryed for a moment and then started again.
questions.tip: The error was “cryed”. A “y” after a consonant changes to “ied”.

questions.q: We was very hungry by twelve o'clock.
Mother had packed sandwichs and a flask of barley water.
questions.tip: The error was “sandwichs”. Words ending in -ch add -es.

questions.q: Everyone eat quietly under the big tree.
questions.tip: The error was “eat”. The story is in the past.

questions.q: It was the goodest picnic we had ever had.
questions.tip: The error was “goodest”. The comparative forms of “good” are “better” and “best”.

sections.name: Booklet B · Comprehension
sections.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions. Note the marks for each question.
sections.passage:
The Letter in the Library Book

I am not the sort of person who finds things. My sister finds coins on the pavement and keys in the drain. I find nothing at all.

So when a folded piece of paper slid out of my library book and onto my lap, I sat very still for a moment.

The book was about volcanoes. I had borrowed it on Tuesday from the school library, and the paper had been tucked between pages forty and forty-one. It was a letter, written in pencil, in handwriting that was rounder and neater than mine.

It said: "To whoever reads this next. I am in Primary 5. This was my favourite book in the whole library and I have borrowed it eleven times. If you like it too, write your name under mine and put the letter back."

Underneath there were four names already.

I read the book twice that week. I learnt that the inside of the earth is hot enough to melt rock, and that a volcano in Indonesia once made a sound heard three thousand kilometres away.

On Friday I took out my pencil. My handwriting is not neat, and for a while I worried about that. Then I wrote my name under the fourth one, folded the letter, and slid it back between pages forty and forty-one.

I returned the book that afternoon.

I still check every library book I borrow now, in case there is something between the pages. There never is. But I keep looking, and I do not mind.

questions.q: What slid out of the library book?
questions.a: A folded piece of paper, which turned out to be a letter written in pencil.

questions.q: What was the book about, and when had the writer borrowed it?
questions.a: It was about volcanoes, and the writer had borrowed it on Tuesday.

questions.q: Where exactly in the book had the letter been tucked?
What did the person who wrote the letter ask the next reader to do?
questions.a: If the reader liked the book too, they should write their name under the writer's and put the letter back in the book.

questions.q: How do we know other children had already followed the instruction?
questions.a: There were four names already written underneath the letter.

questions.q: Give two things the writer learnt from the book.
questions.a: Any two of: the inside of the earth is hot enough to melt rock; a volcano in Indonesia once made a sound that was heard three thousand kilometres away.

questions.q: Why did the writer worry before signing?
questions.a: Because the handwriting in the letter was rounder and neater than the writer's own.

questions.q: Which word in the passage means 'pushed gently into a narrow space'?
The writer says, "I am not the sort of person who finds things." How does the writer show this at the beginning?
questions.a: By comparing himself with his sister, who finds coins on the pavement and keys in the drain, while he finds nothing at all.

questions.q: Why do you think the writer still checks every library book he borrows?
questions.a: Finding the letter was exciting and made him part of something shared with other children, so he hopes to find another. He says he does not mind that there never is one, which shows the looking itself is part of the pleasure.

questions.q: Did the writer enjoy the book? Give one piece of evidence.
questions.a: Yes. Any one of: he read it twice in the same week; he wrote his name under the others, which the letter said to do only if he liked it too.
